name: Anthropic
monetization: Sells Claude models via API, enterprise plans, and Claude Code; the fastest revenue scaling ever recorded in enterprise software, funded by Amazon, Google, and record venture rounds.
description_md: Anthropic is the AI safety-focused lab behind the Claude model family and Claude Code. Its revenue run-rate went from ~$1B (Dec 2024) to ~$9B (Dec 2025) to ~$47B (May 2026) — reportedly passing OpenAI — and its $65B Series H in May 2026 priced it at $965B post-money, the largest private venture round in history. Amazon (~$13B invested, AWS primary training partner) and Google (~$3B equity plus a TPU deal of up to 1M chips) are both major shareholders and compute suppliers.
ai_monetization_md: Predominantly enterprise/API revenue: Claude via API and cloud marketplaces (AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud, and since the Azure deal, Microsoft), enterprise subscriptions, and Claude Code, with consumer subscriptions a smaller share than OpenAI's mix. Run-rate revenue: ~$9B end-2025 → $14B (Feb) → $30B (Apr) → ~$47B (May 2026), per company statements and press. The company has signaled it expects to approach break-even sooner than OpenAI, though no audited figures are public.
ai_strategy_md: Multi-cloud compute at committed scale — >$100B over a decade with AWS including up to 5GW of Trainium, a $30B Azure commitment, up to 1M Google TPUs (>1GW), ~3.5GW of Google-designed TPU capacity via Broadcom from 2027, and a $50B US data-center buildout with Fluidstack — while taking investment from nearly every layer of its own supply chain (Amazon, Google, Microsoft ≤$5B and Nvidia ≤$10B announced Nov 2025; Series H included Blackstone, Brookfield, Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix). Differentiates on enterprise trust, safety research, and coding/agent workloads.
risk_notes_md: The February 2026 federal ban is the defining negative edge: after Anthropic refused to drop acceptable-use limits (mass surveillance, autonomous weapons), all federal agencies were ordered off its products and DoD designated it a supply-chain risk — killing its federal pipeline and pressuring enterprise contractors; Anthropic is litigating and lost an early appeals-court bid (Apr 2026). Other risks: run-rate figures are company/press numbers, not audited; investor-supplier circularity (Amazon booked a ~$53B fair-value gain on its stake in Q2 2026 while selling it compute); compute commitments >$130B across clouds assume the growth curve holds.

observations.notes: Largest private VC round on record; participants reported to include Blackstone, Brookfield, Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix — suppliers investing in their customer.

source.title: Run-rate revenue surpassed $30 billion, up from $9 billion at the end of 2025

observations.notes: Disclosed alongside the Series H; trajectory $9B (Dec 2025) → $14B (Feb) → $19B (Mar) → $30B (Apr) → $47B (May 2026). Reportedly passed OpenAI's run rate. Run rate ≠ recognized revenue.

events.title: Federal agencies ordered to stop using Anthropic products
events.why_it_matters: After Anthropic refused to relax acceptable-use limits for the Pentagon, the President directed all federal agencies to cease using Anthropic AI (some given a six-month transition). Erases Anthropic's federal pipeline and creates compliance risk for contractors — the tracker's canonical negative edge.

events.title: DoD designates Anthropic a supply-chain risk; Anthropic sues
events.why_it_matters: The designation extends the ban's reach into the defense-contractor ecosystem; Anthropic sued DoD and lost an appeals-court bid to temporarily block the ruling (Apr 8, 2026). Litigation outcome determines whether any federal revenue is recoverable.

events.title: Closes $65B Series H at $965B post-money
events.why_it_matters: Largest private venture round in history; makes Anthropic the world's most valuable private AI company, surpassing OpenAI's $852B mark, with supply-chain investors (Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix, Blackstone, Brookfield) in the syndicate.
